html:
The Arapaho are a Native American people of the Plains, who historically lived in what is now Colorado and Wyoming. They speak an Algonquian language, which points to an older homeland further east, before they moved onto the plains.

On the plains they became mounted bison hunters (see horses on the Plains), living in tipis and moving with the herds. They were close allies of the Cheyenne and loosely aligned with the Lakota and Dakota. The French called them Gens de Vache, "cow people", after the bison.

By the 1850s the Arapaho had split into northern and southern tribes. Southern Arapaho were among those killed at the Sand Creek massacre in 1864. Around 1890 Arapaho followers helped spread the Ghost Dance across the plains. Since 1878 the Northern Arapaho have shared the Wind River Reservation in Wyoming with the Eastern Shoshone, once their enemies. The Southern Arapaho live with the Southern Cheyenne in Oklahoma as the Cheyenne and Arapaho Tribes.
